rfm_tuples.R: The Company was in compliance with all covenants, including the financial covenants, under the Senior Credit facility at August 31, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify covenant compliance language in Q1/Q2 FY25 10-Qs; check whether revolver balance increased and whether net-leverage covenant headroom is consistent with disclosed term-loan/cash levels.
rfm_tuples.M_value: $195M term loan, ZERO revolver outstanding at 8/31/2024, $398M revolver available, $167M cash. Net leverage covenant <3.75x, interest coverage >3.00x. Q2 FY25 10-Q (2/28/2025): still ZERO revolver drawn, term loan paid down to $192.5M, $398.5M available, in compliance with all covenants. Implied net leverage ratio is well below 1.0x (term debt $192M / TTM EBITDA ~$135M, net of $167M cash = negative net leverage).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Pristine balance sheet. Net cash position when revolver-undrawn is netted against $167M cash. Covenant compliance is not in question; this is a low-leverage industrial.

rfm_tuples.R: The Company's largest customer accounted for approximately 3% of sales in each of the last three fiscal years.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: Verify segment / Note 15 customer concentration disclosure. Mode B: Look for any single dealer/agent concentration via distributor disclosures; check whether ASCEND/EMEA agent reserve indicates hidden channel concentration.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Largest customer 3% of sales (three-year consistent). Distribution through W.W. Grainger, MSC, Blackwoods (named). However, a $13M reserve was taken in FY22 against a single EMEA agent that was material to that region; the receivable remained fully reserved as of 8/31/2024 and the agent is in bankruptcy. This is a residual Mode B concern (one channel partner failure ~$13M one-time hit absorbed). Otherwise concentration is genuinely low.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Truthful low-concentration disclosure with no evident drift. The previously disclosed EMEA agent issue is fully reserved and isolated; no new agent-receivable problems flagged in Q1/Q2 FY25.

rfm_tuples.R: Through the end of fiscal 2024 when the ASCEND program concluded, the Company has invested approximately $75 million as part of the program... realized approximately $54 million of annual operating profit from execution of the ASCEND program.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: trace ASCEND restructuring/charges schedule across FY22-FY24. Mode B: derive whether the claimed $54M annual operating profit benefit is consistent with reported operating profit trajectory ($31M FY22 -> $84M FY23 -> $122M FY24).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Reported continuing-ops operating profit: $31M (FY22) -> $84M (FY23) -> $122M (FY24). Total OP improvement FY22->FY24 = $91M. ASCEND charges declining each year ($35M -> $7M in SG&A) magnifies the GAAP improvement, but underlying gross margin also expanded 46% -> 51%. The $54M claimed annual run-rate is reasonable given the magnitude of the realized OP improvement. Program is declared concluded with no extension or follow-on restructuring announced; Q2 FY25 confirms zero restructuring charges this year.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: ASCEND claims are corroborated by the reported margin and OP expansion. No evidence of cost-program drift or rolling restructuring. Risk: claim that benefits will be 'maintained' tested by Q1/Q2 FY25 — gross margin slipped 110 bps YoY in H1 FY25 (51.6% -> 50.5%), worth tracking but not yet a violation.

rfm_tuples.R: P. Shannon Burns... was appointed as the Company's Interim Principal Financial Officer by the Board of Directors effective March 1, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: Has the 'Interim' tag been removed since? Track over Q1/Q2 FY25 filings and 8-Ks (Item 5.02) through cutoff.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Executive Officers + Q1/Q2 FY25 Sarbox certs)
rfm_tuples.M_value: As of the 10-K (10/21/2024), the Q1 FY25 10-Q (12/20/2024) and the Q2 FY25 10-Q (3/26/2025), Burns is still signing as 'Interim Principal Financial Officer.' That is ~13 months of 'Interim' status through the cutoff with no permanent CFO appointment 8-K observed. Previous CFO Anthony Colucci departed effective March 1, 2024.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: An 'interim' CFO for ~13 months at a $1.5B+ industrial is a mild yellow flag. Not damning (Burns is an internal hire with FP&A background and EY), but suggests difficulty recruiting or board indecision. Does not impair controls per 9A but is a Mode-B disclosure-by-omission of the underlying CFO succession friction.

rfm_tuples.R: The fiscal 2024 annual review of reporting units performed in the fourth quarter did not result in an impairment. All reporting units exceeded the carrying value by more than 85%.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: trace headroom over multi-year filings. Mode B: Goodwill / intangibles are $306M = 39% of total assets — verify whether IT&S reporting unit pressure is consistent with sales decline.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K critical accounting estimates + EY critical audit matter)
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 headroom >85% (improved from FY23 >65%). EY did flag IT&S goodwill ($256M) as the Critical Audit Matter requiring expanded procedures — consistent with the magnitude, but headroom is broad. FY24 net sales were FLAT (-1% YoY to $590M), but operating profit grew significantly; impairment risk is not signaled in any 8-K through cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Goodwill claim is verifiable and consistent with margin expansion. The CAM disclosure is procedural, not a red flag.

rfm_tuples.R: Ernst & Young LLP (PCAOB ID 42)... In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects... unqualified opinion.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: run auditor_change_tracker to detect any change/resignation/disagreement in the last 5 years.
rfm_tuples.M_value: One auditor change detected (2020-11-19): PwC dismissed, EY appointed. PwC's letter confirmed no disagreements during FY19/FY20. Both firms Big-4. No Big-4 resignations, no disagreements in 5-year window. EY has now signed 4 consecutive clean 10-Ks (FY21-FY24). Signal: UPGRADE_OR_LATERAL.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Lateral Big-4 swap 4+ years ago with explicit no-disagreement letter. Clean, stable auditor relationship. Not a red flag.

rfm_tuples.R: (Cumulative Form 4 insider activity in lookback window approaching FY25 events / share repurchases)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: insider_vs_calendar with cutoff 2025-05-15, window 14 days around budget/CR events. Look for discretionary sales clustered around capital events (acquisitions, debt refis).
rfm_tuples.M_value: 46 Form 4 filings in lookback; 21 sales total; total sale value ~$8.05M over 12 months. Only 1 proximate to a calendar event (CR signing 9/26/2024) — but it is a Code F (tax-withholding on award vesting) by CEO Sternlieb on 10/8/2024 ($933K). Zero discretionary sales near events. Signal: ROUTINE_10B5_1.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Insider activity is dominated by routine tax-withholding (Code F) rather than discretionary open-market sales. CEO sale was non-discretionary tax-share withholding tied to vesting. No insider-event clustering.

rfm_tuples.R: In fiscal 2024, we derived 38% of our net sales from the United States, 29% from Europe, 15% from the Middle East, 10% from Asia and 8% from other geographic areas... Our products and services are generally available globally.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: derive concentration risk — is Saudi/UAE Middle East exposure (15%) a hidden single-country concentration to Saudi Aramco-style oil & gas? Cross-check oil & gas revenue mix.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Note 15 geographic; risk factors on oil & gas)
rfm_tuples.M_value: By geography: US $224M, GB $51M, DE $32M, SA (Saudi) — explicit Saudi disclosure but no $ allocation in geographic breakout (rolled into Middle East 15%). Refinery/petrochemical is listed as a top end-market. Risk factors explicitly call out 'significant portion of our revenues are derived from the sale of products and services to end users in the oil & gas industry.' No specific oil & gas % disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B gap: the Company discloses oil & gas as a material end-market but never quantifies the percentage. Saudi Arabia is broken out as a measurement country but not by absolute revenue. This is an under-disclosure that prevents cleanly forecasting oil-price sensitivity. Not a lie, but informationally thin.

rfm_tuples.R: in fiscal 2019, the Company provided voluntary self-disclosures to both Dutch and U.S. authorities related to sales of products and services linked to the Crimea region of Ukraine, which sales potentially violated European Union and U.S. sanctions provisions... the Company has not adjusted its estimate of financial penalties as a result of the completion of the investigation in the year ended August 31, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: track penalty estimate over multiple years; Mode B: derive whether 'low end of range' reserve is being rolled forward without remeasurement despite a 2022 Dutch Investigator conclusion that EU sanctions were violated.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Crimea sanctions self-disclosure is from FY19 (>5 yrs old). Dutch Investigator concluded VIOLATION in March 2022. Company reserved at 'low end of a reasonable range' in FY21 and has NOT updated the estimate in FY22, FY23, or FY24. US side closed without action. The penalty range and reserve amount are not quantified. This is a Mode-B drift risk: long-tail Dutch prosecutorial decision could land above the reserved range.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosed but not quantified, and unchanged for 3+ years despite an explicit adverse Investigator conclusion. Penalty unlikely to be material to a $590M-revenue / $167M-cash company, but the unchanged 'low end of range' posture is a Mode-B yellow flag — exactly the kind of contingent liability that gets remeasured at settlement.

rfm_tuples.R: On September 4, 2024, the Company acquired 100% of the stock of DTA The Smart Move, S.A. ('DTA')... initial purchase price of $27.2 million plus potential earn-out of EUR 12.0 million... maximum total purchase price of EUR 36.0 million.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify DTA acquisition completed and consolidated. Mode B: derive whether the goodwill assignment (14.5M to IT&S goodwill on $27.2M purchase price = 53% of price to goodwill) is consistent with a bolt-on industrial tuck-in.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K subsequent event Note 17 + Q1 + Q2 FY25 Note on Acquisitions)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q2 FY25 confirms acquisition closed for $27.2M cash, EUR 12M earn-out (3-year tied to financial targets). Goodwill of $14.5M allocated to IT&S in Q2 balance sheet. DTA added ~$6M of sales in H1 FY25 (2% of revenue) and is favorably integrated into HLT product line. No revisions or earn-out remeasurements disclosed. Funded with cash + revolver (revolver back to zero by Q2 end).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Small bolt-on cleanly integrated. Goodwill share is normal for industrial tuck-ins. No earn-out drift. Mode B is satisfied.

summary: EPAC is a well-disclosed, financially conservative specialty-industrial that does not exhibit honesty-alpha red flags. Three years of margin expansion, near-zero net debt, undrawn revolver, fully covenant-compliant, EY clean opinion on both statements and ICFR, lateral Big-4 audit history with no disagreements, low customer concentration (3% top customer), and routine insider activity (tax-withholding-dominated). Only Mode-B yellow flags are: (i) a 13-month 'Interim' CFO designation that has not been resolved, (ii) an FY19 Dutch Crimea-sanctions matter with an unchanged 'low end of range' reserve for 3+ years despite a 2022 adverse Investigator conclusion, and (iii) under-quantified oil & gas / Middle East end-market exposure. None of these rise to severe underdelivery. The pre-cutoff -12.5% drawdown is consistent with macro/cyclical/oil-gas-sensitivity concerns rather than disclosure dishonesty.
